excerpt: Mintlify Workflows lets an AI agent keep your documentation in sync with your code, on a schedule or on every push. How it works, Mintlify pricing and alternatives.
content:
Mintlify is a documentation platform used for developer docs, API references and knowledge bases. Workflows, which Mintlify launched on Product Hunt as "self-updating knowledge bases", is its feature for keeping those docs current without someone remembering to do it. You give an agent a trigger and instructions; when it runs, it checks what changed and either commits a docs update or opens a pull request for your team to review.

Mintlify's own blog describes two kinds of trigger: a push to a repository or branch, and a schedule. Typical jobs it lists are drafting changelogs, catching docs that drifted from the code, checking for broken links, style audits and tracking which translations have fallen behind. Instructions are written in Markdown, so they live in version control with the rest of your docs. On the current pricing page the feature appears as Automations, a Pro and Enterprise feature that costs 250 credits per update and nothing when there is nothing to update.

Mintlify Workflows launched on Product Hunt on 21 May 2026 and finished #2 for the day, with 336 upvotes and 40 comments (as of 14 October 2026). Mintlify itself has 86 reviews on Product Hunt.

We have not tested Mintlify ourselves. This page brings together Mintlify's site, pricing page and blog and its Product Hunt page, and says where each fact comes from.

plans.name: Starter

faq.a: Agent-run jobs that keep Mintlify docs up to date. They run on a push to your repository or on a schedule, and either commit changes or open a pull request for review. The pricing page calls the feature Automations.

faq.q: How much do Mintlify Workflows cost?
faq.a: They need the Pro plan ($450 a month billed annually, or $540 monthly) or Enterprise. Each update uses 250 credits; Pro includes 10,000 credits a month, with overages at $0.01 per credit. A run with nothing to update is free.

faq.q: Is there a free Mintlify plan?
faq.a: Yes. Starter is free for 5 editor seats with a custom domain and the web editor, but it does not include the agent or automations.

faq.q: Will the agent publish changes without review?
faq.a: You choose. Mintlify says changes can be committed directly or opened as a pull request for your team to review.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Mintlify?
faq.a: Product Hunt lists GitBook, Docusaurus, Slite, Notice and Archbee.
